title: Quasi-coherent modules on a Noetherian algebraic space are coherent filtered unions
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Assume $X$ is Noetherian. Modules and quasi-coherence are on the small etale ringed site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Locally Noetherian means that etale scheme charts are locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]; Noetherian means locally Noetherian, quasi-compact and quasi-separated (the diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests). On a locally Noetherian space, coherent means quasi-coherent with coherent pullbacks on all etale scheme charts [pqf-def-coherent]. For every quasi-coherent module $F$ on $X$, the poset of coherent submodules $G\subseteq F$, ordered by inclusion, is a nonempty directed set (in a universe containing the subobjects of $F$), and the canonical map $$\varinjlim_{G\subseteq F,\ G\ \mathrm{coherent}}G\longrightarrow F$$ is an isomorphism of module sheaves. The colimit is in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. The diagram is indexed by a set, not by the category of all coherent modules.

proof.text: Choose a representable surjective etale atlas $p:U\to X$ with $U$ affine by lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas; its quasi-compactness hypothesis holds since $X$ is Noetherian. Put $R=U\times_XU$. By lem-sfb-noetherian-affine-atlas-relation this is a groupoid of Noetherian schemes with $s,t$ flat, quasi-compact and quasi-separated. In particular the relation need not be affine, and no separatedness over the base has been assumed.

Under lem-sfb-space-qcoh-groupoid-equivalence send $F$ to its descent module $(p^*F,\alpha_F)$. Apply lem-sfb-flat-noetherian-groupoid-coherent-approximation: step 1 checked both Noetherian schemes and all three properties of each projection. We get a small filtered diagram of coherent groupoid modules and a colimit cocone to this descent module. Apply the inverse equivalence to obtain a diagram $H_i$ in $\operatorname{QCoh}(X)$ with coherent terms, and cocone maps $h_i:H_i\to F$. The equivalence identifies the compatible maps out of these terms on both sides, so the universal property of this cocone gives $F=\operatorname{colim}_iH_i$ in QCoh. By lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits this is also the colimit in all module sheaves.

Let $P$ be the poset of actual coherent subsheaves of $F$. It is a set in the stipulated universe: on a small skeleton of the site, each subsheaf specifies a subset of each section set of $F$, and the compatible choices form a subset of the product of their power sets. The zero subsheaf is coherent and belongs to $P$. For $G,H\in P$, their sum $G\oplus H$ is quasi-coherent by lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits. Its restriction to the atlas corresponds to the sum of the coherent scheme modules $p^*G,p^*H$, which is coherent by lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth. Coherence detection in lem-sfb-space-qcoh-groupoid-equivalence gives coherence of $G\oplus H$. Its image in $F$ is quasi-coherent by lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits, and a quotient of the coherent module $G\oplus H$, hence coherent by lem-sfb-space-noetherian-coherent-support. This image contains both $G$ and $H$, so $P$ is nonempty and directed.

Form $C=\operatorname{colim}_{G\in P}G$ with its canonical map $a:C\to F$. By lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful it is the module sheafification of the sectionwise colimit. For every site object $V$, the sectionwise colimit of this directed diagram of inclusions is the submodule $\bigcup_{G\in P}G(V)\subseteq F(V)$: two representatives have equal images exactly when their images in a common upper bound agree. Thus this presheaf maps injectively into $F$. Exact module sheafification, as stated by lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-sheafification-exact, preserves its kernel zero. Consequently $a$ is a monomorphism.

For each $h_i:H_i\to F$ let $K_i$ be its image. It is quasi-coherent by lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits and coherent by the quotient clause of lem-sfb-space-noetherian-coherent-support, since $H_i$ is coherent. Hence $K_i\in P$ and $h_i$ factors as $H_i\twoheadrightarrow K_i\hookrightarrow F$. Compose the first map with $K_i\to C$ to obtain $b_i:H_i\to C$. For any transition $u:i\to j$, the maps $b_jH(u)$ and $b_i$ have equal composites with $a$, namely $h_i$, and are equal because step 4 proved $a$ monic. Thus the $b_i$ form a cocone. The ambient colimit property from step 2 gives $b:F\to C$ with $b h_i=b_i$. The equality $ab=1_F$ follows after composition with every $h_i$ and the uniqueness in that colimit property. Since $a$ is monic, $a(ba)=a$ implies $ba=1_C$. Therefore the canonical map $a$ is an isomorphism.

lean.statement: theorem coherentSubobjects_filtered_colimit {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (hln : ∀ T : X.EtaleSite, IsLocallyNoetherian (X.etaleForget.obj T)) (hqc : CompactSpace (Point X.obj.obj)) (hqs : ∀ (U V : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X.obj.obj) (b : yoneda.obj V ⟶ X.obj.obj), IsAffine U.left → IsAffine V.left → CompactSpace (Point (Limits.pullback a b))) (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] : Nonempty (CoherentSubobjects F) ∧ IsDirected (CoherentSubobjects F) (· ≤ ·) ∧ ∃ c : ColimitCocone (coherentSubobjectDiagram F), IsIso (c.isColimit.desc (coherentSubobjectCocone F))
lean.note: Finite presentation on the small etale ringed site is exactly coherence on a locally Noetherian algebraic space by Stacks 07UB (equivalence (1),(3),(4)). Absolute quasi-separatedness uses the affine-pair test of 0AHR, without imposing quasi-separatedness of the structure morphism alone. The conclusion supplies an actual colimit cocone and asserts that its canonical comparison to F is an isomorphism, so no large-colimit existence is added as a hypothesis.
